test_cases.title: Valid document classification with confidence score
test_cases.preconditions: The service is running and accessible. A valid document file is available for testing.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid document file (e.g., a PDF or text file) that clearly belongs to one of the 12 defined categories.

steps.action: Submit the valid document to the classification service.
steps.expected: The service returns a response with a predicted category that is one of the 12 defined categories.

steps.action: Verify the confidence score in the response.
steps.expected: The confidence score is a numeric value between 0 and 1 (inclusive).

test_cases.title: Boundary test for confidence score minimum value
test_cases.preconditions: The service is running. A document is available that is expected to yield a very low confidence score (e.g., an ambiguous or mixed-content document).
test_cases.test_inputs: A document that is ambiguous or contains mixed content to potentially yield a low confidence score.

steps.action: Submit the ambiguous document to the classification service.
steps.expected: The service returns a response with a predicted category.

steps.action: Verify the confidence score is not below 0.
steps.expected: The confidence score is greater than or equal to 0.

test_cases.title: Boundary test for confidence score maximum value
test_cases.preconditions: The service is running. A document is available that is expected to yield a very high confidence score (e.g., a clear, unambiguous document of a specific category).
test_cases.test_inputs: A document that is clear and unambiguous, strongly belonging to one specific category.

steps.action: Submit the clear document to the classification service.
steps.expected: The service returns a response with a predicted category.

steps.action: Verify the confidence score is not above 1.
steps.expected: The confidence score is less than or equal to 1.

test_cases.title: Invalid file format handling
test_cases.preconditions: The service is running. An invalid file (e.g., a corrupted file or unsupported format) is available.
test_cases.test_inputs: An invalid or unsupported file format (e.g., a corrupted PDF or a binary file that is not a document).

steps.action: Submit the invalid file to the classification service.
steps.expected: The service returns an error response indicating the file could not be processed.

steps.action: Verify that no classification result is returned for the invalid file.
steps.expected: The response does not contain a predicted category or confidence score.

test_cases.title: Document with confidence score below 0.60 is routed to human review
test_cases.preconditions: The system is running and a document is available for processing.
test_cases.test_inputs: A document that results in a confidence score of 0.55.
test_cases.assumptions: The classification engine outputs a confidence score between 0.0 and 1.0.

steps.action: Submit the document for classification.
steps.expected: The document is processed and the confidence score is calculated as 0.55.

steps.action: Check the destination of the document.
steps.expected: The document is routed to the human review queue and not classified automatically.

test_cases.title: Document with confidence score exactly 0.60 is classified automatically
test_cases.preconditions: The system is running and a document is available for processing.
test_cases.test_inputs: A document that results in a confidence score of exactly 0.60.

steps.action: Submit the document for classification.
steps.expected: The document is processed and the confidence score is calculated as 0.60.

steps.action: Check the destination of the document.
steps.expected: The document is classified automatically and not routed to the human review queue.

test_cases.title: Document with confidence score significantly below 0.60 is routed to human review
test_cases.preconditions: The system is running and a document is available for processing.
test_cases.test_inputs: A document that results in a confidence score of 0.10.

steps.action: Submit the document for classification.
steps.expected: The document is processed and the confidence score is calculated as 0.10.

steps.action: Check the destination of the document.
steps.expected: The document is routed to the human review queue and not classified automatically.

test_cases.title: 95th percentile response time under 50 rps load
test_cases.preconditions: The Document Classification Service is deployed and operational. A load testing tool capable of generating sustained load and recording response times is available. A dataset of valid document files suitable for classification is prepared.
test_cases.test_inputs: A set of valid document files (e.g., 1000 unique PDFs or text files) to be used for requests.
test_cases.assumptions: The test environment is isolated from production traffic. The load generator can sustain exactly 50 requests per second. The definition of 'request' is a single HTTP POST/GET call to the classification endpoint with a valid document payload. Response time is measured from request initiation to the first byte of the response or full response receipt (standard definition for such SLAs).

steps.action: Initiate a load test that sends classification requests to the service at a constant rate of 50 requests per second for a duration sufficient to collect a statistically significant sample of response times (e.g., 5 minutes, resulting in 15,000 requests).
steps.expected: The load test completes successfully without the service crashing or becoming unresponsive. A log of response times for all successful requests is generated.

steps.action: Calculate the 95th percentile of the recorded response times from the load test results.
steps.expected: The calculated 95th percentile response time is less than or equal to 500 ms.

test_cases.title: Verification of top three contributing passages for a document
test_cases.preconditions: The Document Classification Service is running and accessible.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text document containing at least four distinct sentences or paragraphs.
test_cases.assumptions: The service returns a structured response (e.g., JSON) containing a list of passages and their contribution scores.

steps.action: Submit the test document to the classification service.
steps.expected: The service returns a successful classification response.

steps.action: Inspect the response for the list of contributing passages.
steps.expected: The response contains exactly three text passages identified as the most contributing.

steps.action: Verify the content of the returned passages.
steps.expected: Each of the three passages corresponds to a substring of the original input document.

test_cases.title: Verification of contributing passages for a short document
test_cases.preconditions: The Document Classification Service is running and accessible.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text document containing exactly three distinct sentences.
test_cases.assumptions: The service treats each sentence as a distinct passage candidate.

steps.action: Submit the short test document to the classification service.
steps.expected: The service returns a successful classification response.

steps.action: Inspect the response for the list of contributing passages.
steps.expected: The response contains exactly three text passages.

steps.action: Verify the content of the returned passages.
steps.expected: The three returned passages match the three sentences in the input document.

test_cases.title: Verification of contributing passages for a document with fewer than three distinct segments
test_cases.preconditions: The Document Classification Service is running and accessible.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text document containing only one single sentence.
test_cases.assumptions: The service defines a 'passage' as a sentence or paragraph; if fewer than three distinct passages exist, it may return fewer or handle it gracefully.

steps.action: Submit the single-sentence test document to the classification service.
steps.expected: The service processes the request without crashing.

steps.action: Inspect the response for the list of contributing passages.
steps.expected: The service either returns the single available passage or returns an empty list/error message, but does not return duplicate entries to fake three passages.

test_cases.title: Offline functionality verification
test_cases.preconditions: The Field Triage Tablet Application is installed and configured on a tablet device with network connectivity disabled (e.g., Airplane Mode enabled or Wi-Fi/Ethernet disconnected).
test_cases.assumptions: The definition of 'fully functional' includes the ability to create, view, edit, and delete casualty records, as well as access existing local data, without requiring a server connection.

steps.action: Verify that the network connectivity is disabled on the tablet device.
steps.expected: The device status bar or system settings indicate no active network connection.

steps.action: Launch the Field Triage Tablet Application.
steps.expected: The application starts successfully and displays the main interface without error messages related to connectivity.

steps.action: Navigate to the casualty record creation screen and enter valid data for a new casualty.
steps.expected: The form accepts the input and the 'Save' button is enabled.

steps.action: Save the new casualty record.
steps.expected: The record is saved successfully, a success message is displayed, and the new record appears in the local list.

steps.action: Open the saved casualty record and modify a field (e.g., change triage status).
steps.expected: The modification is accepted and saved locally without any network-related errors.

steps.action: Delete the modified casualty record.
steps.expected: The record is removed from the local list and a confirmation message is displayed.

test_cases.title: Local storage capacity for 500 casualty records
test_cases.preconditions: The Field Triage Tablet Application is running offline. The local database is empty or has been cleared of previous test data.
test_cases.assumptions: A standard casualty record structure is used for the test data. The storage limit refers to the number of records, not file size, as specified by '500 casualty records'.

steps.action: Create 499 unique casualty records using a script or manual entry with distinct identifiers.
steps.expected: All 499 records are created and saved successfully to the local storage.

steps.action: Create the 500th casualty record.
steps.expected: The 500th record is created and saved successfully. The application does not display a storage full error.

steps.action: Verify the total count of casualty records in the local database or list view.
steps.expected: The system reports exactly 500 records stored locally.

test_cases.title: Behavior when exceeding 500 local casualty records
test_cases.preconditions: The Field Triage Tablet Application is running offline. The local database already contains exactly 500 casualty records.
test_cases.assumptions: The requirement 'store at least 500' implies that the system must handle the state of having 500 records. It does not explicitly define behavior for the 501st record, but a robust system should either allow it (if 'at least' implies no hard cap at 500) or provide a clear error/management mechanism. Given the phrasing 'store at least 500', it is a minimum capacity guarantee. However, in test engineering, we often test the boundary of 'minimum' to see if it fails gracefully or if the 'at least' is interpreted as a hard limit in some contexts. If the system allows more than 500, it meets the requirement. If it blocks it, it also meets the requirement (since it stored 500). The test here verifies that the system does not crash or corrupt data when attempting to exceed the verified minimum capacity.

steps.action: Attempt to create the 501st casualty record.
steps.expected: Either the record is saved successfully (indicating capacity is greater than 500) OR a specific error message is displayed indicating storage limits or requiring data management, without the application crashing or corrupting existing data.

steps.action: Verify the integrity of the existing 500 records.
steps.expected: The existing 500 records remain intact and accessible.

test_cases.test_inputs: Local records: R1 (ID: 101), R2 (ID: 102). Server status: Online.
test_cases.assumptions: The application has a mechanism to detect connectivity restoration.

steps.action: Restore network connectivity to the server.
steps.expected: The application initiates the synchronization process.

steps.action: Wait for the synchronization process to complete.
steps.expected: Local records R1 and R2 are transmitted to the server and marked as synchronized in the local database.

test_cases.title: Conflict resolution keeping both versions for manual review
test_cases.preconditions: A conflict exists where a local record (ID: 201, Field 'Severity': 'Critical') has been modified while the server version (ID: 201, Field 'Severity': 'Moderate') was also modified during the offline period. Connectivity is restored.
test_cases.test_inputs: Local Record 201: Severity='Critical'. Server Record 201: Severity='Moderate'.
test_cases.assumptions: The system identifies concurrent edits to the same record field as a conflict.

steps.action: Restore network connectivity to the server.

steps.expected: Both versions of the record (Local: 'Critical', Server: 'Moderate') are preserved and displayed in a state requiring manual review. No version is automatically discarded or overwritten.

steps.expected: Local records remain unsynchronized. The application does not delete or modify local data. An error or warning indicating synchronization failure is displayed.

steps.action: Check the battery status after 8 hours of operation.
steps.expected: The battery level is greater than 0%, and the tablet has not powered off.

test_cases.title: Battery endurance verification at boundary limit
test_cases.preconditions: The tablet battery is fully charged (100%). The 'defined usage profile' configuration is active.
test_cases.assumptions: The 'defined usage profile' represents the maximum expected sustained load for the application.

steps.action: Start the defined usage profile on the fully charged tablet.

steps.action: Monitor the battery level continuously until it reaches a critical threshold (e.g., 10-15%) or the 8-hour mark, whichever comes first.
steps.expected: If the battery reaches a critical threshold before 8 hours, the system should provide a low battery warning. If the 8-hour mark is reached before critical threshold, the device must still be functional.

steps.action: Verify the device state exactly at the 8-hour mark.
steps.expected: The device is still powered on and the application is operational, confirming it meets the 'at least 8 hours' requirement.

test_cases.preconditions: Ağ geçidi çalışıyor ve yapılandırılmış günlük sistemi aktif durumdadır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Bilinen bir istemci kimliği ile tek bir HTTP isteği.

steps.action: Bilinen bir istemci kimliği kullanılarak tek bir HTTP isteği gönderilir.
steps.expected: İstek başarılı bir şekilde yanıtlanır.

steps.action: Günlük kaydına erişilir ve ilgili istek için kayıt arandığında izleme kimliği (trace ID) ve istemci kimliği alanları kontrol edilir.
steps.expected: Kayıtta benzersiz bir izleme kimliği ve gönderilen istemci kimliği doğru şekilde yer alır.

test_cases.title: Uç nokta, yanıt kodu ve süre bilgisinin günlük kaydına yazılması
test_cases.preconditions: Ağ geçidi çalışıyor ve yapılandırılmış günlük sistemi aktif durumdadır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Bilinen bir uç noktaya (ör. /api/v1/data) gönderilen tek bir HTTP isteği.

steps.action: Belirli bir uç noktaya (ör. /api/v1/data) HTTP isteği gönderilir ve yanıt kodu gözlemlenir.
steps.expected: İstek yanıtlanır (ör. HTTP 200).

steps.action: Günlük kaydındaki ilgili girişte uç nokta, yanıt kodu ve süre alanları kontrol edilir.
steps.expected: Uç nokta değeri gönderilen yol ile eşleşir, yanıt kodu gözlemlenen kod ile eşleşir ve süre alanı 0'dan büyük bir değer içerir.

test_cases.title: Hata durumundaki isteklerin günlük kaydına yazılması
test_cases.preconditions: Ağ geçidi çalışıyor ve yapılandırılmış günlük sistemi aktif durumdadır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Geçersiz bir uç noktaya gönderilen HTTP isteği.

steps.action: Var olmayan bir uç noktaya (ör. /api/v1/invalid) HTTP isteği gönderilir.
steps.expected: İstek HTTP 404 veya ilgili hata kodu ile yanıtlanır.

steps.action: Günlük kaydındaki ilgili girişte izleme kimliği, istemci kimliği, uç nokta, yanıt kodu ve süre alanları kontrol edilir.
steps.expected: Kayıt mevcuttur, yanıt kodu hata kodunu (ör. 404) içerir, diğer alanlar doğru şekilde doludur.

test_cases.title: Configuration change application without restart
test_cases.preconditions: The API Gateway is running with a baseline configuration. A test endpoint is available.
test_cases.test_inputs: A new configuration value (e.g., changing a timeout value or adding a new route) that is valid for the gateway.
test_cases.assumptions: The gateway supports dynamic configuration reloading via its API or file watcher mechanism as per standard implementation.

steps.action: Apply a valid configuration change to the running gateway instance.
steps.expected: The gateway accepts the configuration change without requiring a process restart.

steps.action: Send a request to the gateway that utilizes the changed configuration.
steps.expected: The request is processed according to the new configuration values.

test_cases.title: In-flight requests preserved during configuration change
test_cases.preconditions: The API Gateway is running. A long-running request (e.g., with a delay of at least 5 seconds) is initiated to the backend.
test_cases.test_inputs: A configuration change command triggered while the long-running request is active.
test_cases.assumptions: The backend service can simulate a delayed response to ensure the request remains in-flight.

steps.action: Initiate a request to the gateway that will take a significant amount of time to complete (in-flight).
steps.expected: The request is accepted and processing begins.

steps.action: Apply a configuration change to the gateway while the request from step 1 is still in-flight.
steps.expected: The configuration change is applied successfully.

steps.action: Wait for the completion of the request initiated in step 1.
steps.expected: The request completes successfully with the expected response, indicating it was not dropped.
